title: BECE English Studies: Grammar & Structure - English Studies - Tenses
subject: English Studies

questions.q:
Choose the correct verb tense to complete the sentence:
"I _____ in this city for ten years."
questions.explain: The phrase 'for ten years' indicates an action that started in the past and continues into the present (or is recently completed with present relevance). This requires the present perfect tense 'have lived'.
questions.subject: English Studies

questions.q: Which sentence correctly uses the past perfect tense?
options: The train left before we arrived at the station.
The train has left before we arrived at the station.
The train had left before we arrived at the station.
The train was leaving before we arrived at the station.
questions.explain: The past perfect tense is formed with 'had' + past participle. It is used to show that one action happened before another action in the past. 'Had left' indicates the train left before the arrival happened.
questions.subject: English Studies

questions.q:
Choose the correct verb tense for the sentence:
"By the end of next month, we _____ all the topics in the syllabus."
questions.explain: The phrase 'By the end of next month' sets a deadline in the future before which an action will be completed. This requires the future perfect tense: 'will have' + past participle.
questions.subject: English Studies

questions.q:
Which option completes the sentence correctly to show a past interrupted action?
"The guests _____ dinner when the host finally arrived."
questions.explain: The past continuous tense ('were eating') is used to describe an ongoing action in the past that was interrupted by a shorter action in the simple past ('arrived').
questions.subject: English Studies

questions.q:
Which verb form correctly completes the sentence?
"We _____ here for the bus since 8 AM."
questions.explain: The use of 'since 8 AM' indicates an action that started in the past and is still continuing. This requires the present perfect continuous tense: 'have been waiting'.
questions.subject: English Studies

questions.q:
Select the correct tense for the sentence:
"By the time the guests arrived, she _____ cooking dinner."
questions.explain: The sentence describes an action in the past (cooking dinner) that was completed before another action in the past (the guests arrived). The past perfect tense ('had finished') is used for the earlier action.
questions.subject: English Studies

questions.q:
Which option completes the sentence using the past perfect tense?
"Before the police arrived at the scene, the criminals _____."
questions.explain: To indicate that one past action occurred before another past action, we use the past perfect tense ('had' + past participle) for the earlier action.
questions.subject: English Studies
